papers_read.title_as_printed: Hippocampal auto-segmentation based on deep learning for identifying magnetic resonance imaging biomarkers of early mild cognitive impairment (Hu, Ma, Zheng, Ma, Xia; Neuroscience 591 (2025) 76-82)
Machine learning approaches to mild cognitive impairment detection based on structural MRI data and morphometric features (Zubrikhina et al., Cognitive Systems Research 78 (2023) 87-95)

what_each_reports.P-52: Deep-learning (U-Net/CNN) hippocampal auto-segmentation, 1183 radiomic features reduced to 7 (Spearman filter + LASSO), XGBoost; single-centre Wenzhou Seventh People's Hospital cohort, 105 MCI vs 45 NC (MoCA/MMSE education-adjusted cut-offs), random 7:3 split: training AUC 0.935 (95% CI 0.83-0.97), test set (30 MCI, 15 NC) AUC 0.864 (95% CI 0.73-0.89). No accuracy reported in the text.
what_each_reports.P-99: FreeSurfer 6.0.1 morphometry (906 features), chi-squared SelectKBest, RBF SVC; Moscow memory-clinic cohort, 145 MCI (ICD-10 F06.7, over 65) vs 62 healthy volunteers, 10-fold CV: accuracy 0.73 +/- 0.059, ROC-AUC 0.735 +/- 0.076, F1-macro 0.683 (Table 1).

quantity_a: Held-out test ROC-AUC (45 subjects) of an XGBoost classifier on seven hippocampal radiomic features, MCI vs NC, single Chinese hospital cohort, 3D T1.
quantity_b: 10-fold CV accuracy (recorded) / ROC-AUC of an RBF SVC on FreeSurfer whole-brain morphometry, MCI vs HC, single Moscow memory-clinic cohort, 1.5T T1.
incompatible_if_same: No. The record sets an AUC against an accuracy. Comparing AUC with AUC, P-99's 0.735 +/- 0.076 sits at the lower bound of P-52's printed test interval (0.73-0.89), so the uncertainty does not exclude it; neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match: both MCI vs normal controls from baseline T1 MRI (T1).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: P-52 is a Wenzhou hospital cohort, P-99 a Moscow memory-clinic cohort; no shared dataset. The record's 'dataset_equal: Yes' matched the registry placeholder 'not reported' held by both rows. No waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: match in tier: internal validation only in both (random held-out split vs 10-fold CV).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded (AUC vs accuracy); the populations behind 'MCI' differ (MoCA/MMSE cut-offs in a Chinese hospital vs ICD-10 F06.7 diagnoses over age 65), and so do the predictors (seven hippocampal radiomic texture features vs 906 FreeSurfer morphometric features).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.864 and 0.73 are well below 0.97.
independence: Distinct studies, sites, countries and authors; no shared data.
grounds: The dataset-family gate fails with no waiver: P-52 is a Wenzhou hospital cohort and P-99 a Moscow memory-clinic cohort, and the recorded 'Yes' matched only the shared registry placeholder 'not reported'.
The recorded claims are on different metric types (P-52 AUC 0.864 vs P-99 accuracy 73%).
Predictors and MCI definitions differ (hippocampal radiomics vs FreeSurfer morphometry; cut-off-defined MCI vs ICD-10 F06.7), the representation confound of precedents C-80 and C-01.
Even on a common AUC scale the results overlap: P-99's 0.735 lies at the lower edge of P-52's printed 0.73-0.89 test interval.

evidence_quotes.quote: The XGBoost model, utilizing the seven selected features, achieved the highest AUC in the test set (AUC = 0.864, 95 %CI:0.73–0.89).
This study was conducted at Wenzhou Seventh People’s Hospital, between May 2020 and June 2024.
an independent test set that contained 30 MCI patients and 15 NC subjects.
First, the relatively small sample size and lack of external validation may constrain the generalizability of our findings.
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the «Memory Clinic» (Moscow, Russia).
Patients over the age of 65 who had been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (F06.7) were eligible.
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)

record_defects: dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong: the two cohorts are separate single-site clinical samples in China and Russia; the match came from both registry rows holding 'not reported'.

The resolution-evidence list mixes metrics and tasks (e.g. P-411 PD-MCI accuracy, P-416 precision, P-538 three-class qEEG/ERP AUC) and names no separating condition; 'partially resolved' is unsupported.

P-52 note (not in the record): its NC group is described as MoCA >=27 yet Table 1 gives NC MoCA 22.53 +/- 2.91 with no significant MCI/NC MoCA difference (p = 0.17), and its printed test CI (0.73-0.89) is asymmetric about 0.864; these internal inconsistencies weaken P-52's estimate further.
what_would_change_the_verdict: The two feature sets evaluated on one shared cohort, or the same pipeline evaluated on both cohorts, with non-overlapping AUC intervals.
